title: Architecture Standards: Integrated Guidelines and ADRs
author: Jordan Kim
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and standards across API, coding, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also records the active Decision Records (ADRs) that govern cross-cutting choices. The goal is a single reference that engineering teams can rely on for consistent, production-grade design and implementation.

Scope

- Applies to all public and internal services owned by Redwood Inference engineering orgs.
- Includes hosted API, Dedicated components, and Private deployment controls.
- Excludes prototype / research notebooks (see eng-research wiki).

Decision Records (ADRs)

Active ADRs (representative):
1. ADR-2024-01: Default transport: HTTP/2 + gRPC for internal service-to-service calls. Rationale: multiplexing, flow control, and efficient streaming support.
2. ADR-2025-04: Model artifacts: ONNX and a standard model-metadata.json for serving metadata. Rationale: portability and toolchain compatibility.
3. ADR-2026-02: Quantized model variants: prefer 4-bit symmetric quantization for production CPU/GPU inference where supported.
4. ADR-2026-07: Routing policy: latency-first for interactive routes, cost-first for batch/embeddings.

Each ADR contains: title, status, date, owner, decision, consequences, and rollback plan. ADR templates are in the Appendix.

API Standards

Principles:
- Backwards compatibility: new fields must be additive and opt-in via versioning.
- Consistency: resource names and error codes consistent across services.
- Explicit contracts: JSON Schema or Protobuf for all public endpoints.

Conventions:
- Use OpenAPI 3.1 for REST endpoints; generate server + client stubs.
- gRPC for high-throughput internal RPCs; shielded behind REST facade for customers.
- Endpoint naming: /v{MAJOR}/{resource}/{id} e.g., /v1/models/{model_id}/infer.
- Standard error response (JSON):
  {
    "error_code": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "request_id": "string",
    "details": ["string"]
  }

Versioning policy:
- MAJOR increments for breaking changes.
- MINOR for backward-compatible feature additions.
- PATCH for bug fixes.
- Deprecation: announce 90 days before removal for customer-facing endpoints.

Coding Standards

General rules:
- Language-specific style guides: follow PEP8 for Python, Google Java style for Java, and Rustfmt/Clippy for Rust components.
- All services must include unit tests with >= 80% coverage on critical paths and integration tests for external contracts.
- Use typed interfaces where available (TypeScript, Python type hints, gRPC protos).

Repository layout and monorepo guidance:
- Service boundaries in dedicated packages/modules.
- Shared libraries in /libs with clear public API and changelog.
- No circular dependencies.

Security and secrets:
- Never commit secrets. Use Vault/KMS and env-based injection in CI/CD.
- Crypto operations via vetted libraries only.

Infrastructure Standards

Provisioning & IaC:
- Terraform (recommended) for cloud infra; modules must be published and versioned in the infra registry.
- All changes require plan files in PR and automated terraform fmt/tflint checks.

Networking & tenancy:
- VPC per environment (prod/staging/dev).
- Service-to-service access controlled via mTLS; use service mesh for policy if latency budget allows.

Capacity and cost controls:
- Define capacity zones with autoscaling policies; baseline capacity and burst limits must be in code.
- Tagging: every resource must include tags: owner, cost_center, environment, project.

Model-serving Standards

Model packaging and metadata:
- Package: model.bin + tokenizer + model-metadata.json. model-metadata.json fields: model_id, version, architecture, supported_sequences, quantization_profile, input_schema, output_schema, created_by, checksum.
- Example model-metadata.json (stringified):
  {"model_id":"redwood-7b-v1","version":"2026-03-01","architecture":"transformer","supported_sequences":"4096","quantization_profile":"q4_sym","input_schema":"text","output_schema":"text","created_by":"model-onboarding"}

Serving topology:
- Primary serving via GPU clusters for heavy models; CPU shards for small embeddings and low-cost variants.
- KV cache layer for prefix caching; TTLs configurable per-model.
- Auto-fallback: if preferred model variant unavailable, route to nearest compatible variant per ADR-2026-07.

Quality & regressions:
- All model rollouts require an eval suite (prompt set + automated metrics).
- Regression guardrails: compare baseline metrics (perplexity, ROUGE, task-specific AUC) with predefined thresholds; block rollout if metrics degrade > configured delta.

Observability Standards

Metrics:
- Use Prometheus-compatible metrics. Standard buckets: request_latency_ms (histogram), tokens_generated_total (counter), model_cache_hit_ratio (gauge), active_sessions (gauge), error_count_total (counter by code).
- SLO-derived metrics must be exported with labels: route, model_id, region, tier.

Tracing & logs:
- Distributed tracing using OpenTelemetry. Trace every external request end-to-end, include model_id and request_id.
- Structured logs (JSON) with keys: timestamp, level, service, request_id, model_id, route, message, extras. Logs forwarded to ELK/observability pipeline with 90-day retention for prod.

Alerting:
- Alert fatigue control: critical alerts only for SLO breaches, severe errors, and capacity exhaustion. Use aggregated alerts (per-service) and runbook links.

Performance Standards

SLOs (default guidelines):
| Route Type        | P95 Latency | P99 Latency | Error rate (5m) | Throughput target | Notes |
|-------------------|-------------|-------------|-----------------|-------------------|-------|
| Interactive (chat)| 120 ms      | 350 ms      | <0.1%           | scale to 200 rps   | measured at gateway
| Generation (long) | 500 ms      | 1200 ms     | <0.5%           | batch-friendly     | token streaming
| Embeddings         | 50 ms       | 150 ms      | <0.05%          | high qps           | CPU-optimized

Benchmarking & testing:
- Every model and serving config must publish: throughput (tokens/s), p95/p99 latency at defined sequence lengths, and GPU/CPU utilization at target QPS.
- Use synthetic and replayed production traces for load tests.

Performance optimization levers (ordered):
1. Batching and adaptive micro-batching.
2. KV/prefix caching.
3. Quantized model variants.
4. Kernel tuning and sequence bucketing.
5. Autoscaling / dedicated capacity adjustments.

Rollout, Exceptions, and Governance

- Rollouts: Canary at 1% traffic for 24h, evaluate metrics and logs, then ramp to 10% for 12h, then to 100% if no regressions.
- Emergency rollback: route all traffic to previous stable model or fallback service; follow incident runbook.
- Exceptions: require ADR or architecture review board approval; document reason, mitigations, and expiration.

Implementation Plan and Ownership

- Owners: API standards (API Platform team), Coding standards (Eng DX), Infra standards (Eng Infra), Model-serving (Serving Runtime), Observability (Platform), Performance (SRE).
- Roadmap: prioritized crawl-walk-run items for next 6 months:
  1) Publish standardized model-metadata.json schema and validators.
  2) Add OpenAPI enforcement in CI for all public services.
  3) Promote standard Prometheus metrics and dashboards.
  4) ADR backlog clean-up and publish canonical ADR registry.

Appendix: Templates and Examples

ADR template (use for new decisions):
- Title
- Status (proposed/accepted/archived)
- Date
- Owner
- Context
- Decision
- Consequences
- Rollback plan

CI checklist (must pass before merge):
1. Lint & format checks
2. Unit tests & integration smoke tests
3. Security scan (SAST)
4. OpenAPI / proto validation
5. Terraform plan (for infra changes)

Model metadata quick reference (fields):
- model_id, version, architecture, max_sequence_length, quantization_profile, tokenizer_spec, input_schema, output_schema, evaluation_baseline, created_by, checksum.
